note: Widget motion-program interpreter (28 opcodes via table 0x34d3a0; times in 1/60 s): property ramps (e.g. op 0x13 alpha to a target over N frames), waits, loops, end. Called by the widget update slots 0x24ccc/0x25398/0x261e8. The web re-implements the few programs it needs per screen (CSS/JS); the flowchart cursor flash (0x34b7f0) is not reproduced. Fixed 2026-11-07 (checklist G16): every ramp is linear: an op (e.g. op 12 at 0x2014c, op 19 at 0x20420) sets a channel's base (the property now), delta, time 0, speed 1 and acceleration 0, and each frame the value is base + delta x time / (frames / 60) until time reaches it; op 2 ends the program. Op 19 is the alpha (to the entry's value), op 12 adds the entry's value to the x scale. Programs 0x337380 / 0x34b7f0 (op 19 to -1 over 30 frames: drawn 15 frames, as 0x254bc skips alpha 0 or less) and 0x3372d8 (op 12, +1 over 12 frames) are gallery.js cgCursorLight and the column line. Test G16.

Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2, traced twice): Stores bit 0 of the 0xa7f60 result at text object +0x18a91 (whole message or letter by letter colouring), called by 0xa7790 once per set-up. textbox.js:colourMarks computes the same choice as byLetter: a @c1-5 after visible text (spaces and U+3000 not counted), or @r after a colour mark.

feature: tag callbacks
note: Stores the inline tag callbacks (0xa7eb0 / 0xa7f30 slots).

feature: mark scan
note: Tests the stored text for an @ mark (re-layout on resize).

feature: glyph ids for marks
note: Stores two special glyph ids (0x8f/0x90 lookups) and a count.

feature: sample letters reset
note: Zeroes letter alphas and sets the front (config samples).

feature: per-letter colour
note: Colours a letter from the last run at or before it, with its alpha. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2, traced twice): Per-letter colour and alpha: whole-message text writes white per letter (the colour is applied at draw); letter by letter takes the last run at or before the letter, run colour 0 being the base colour, table 0x3c99d2 otherwise; alpha is written as int(a x 255). textbox.js colourMarks / parseMarkup / fillSegment give the same result with .color1-5 spans from each mark and letterAlpha. The effect branches of +0x18a68 are set only by @a, which no script uses.

feature: text measuring
glyph preparation
note: Splits the text into glyph strings for drawing and measuring.

feature: row breaking
note: Breaks rows by cell count and kinsoku; deliberately replaced by browser wrapping. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2, traced twice): Finds where a row breaks by cell count and the kinsoku sets (+0x18da0, +0x18da8), stopping at code 10 and the 0x10 / 0x11 width codes. Part of the monospaced layout recorded as deliberately not adopted (NATIVE-PARITY.md:99-101); browser wrapping with the breaks reflow.js keeps takes its place.

feature: single-width cells (patched)
note: Cell width per character (patched: ASCII and private-use single width); the web uses proportional glyphs. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2, traced twice): The patched test at its head returns single width for code points up to 0x100 and 0xE000-0xF000 (listing 0xc4dd8-0xc4e04), which 0xbdc2c uses for the 0x10 / 0x11 width codes; the rest rewrites the buffer for row breaks. Cell widths are the monospaced layout recorded as deliberately not adopted (NATIVE-PARITY.md:99-101); the port uses proportional glyphs (style.css --story-font).

feature: line feeds (patched)
note: Line-feed handling inside the layout (patched spots 0xc5a18/0xc5a24); the web keeps the break characters reflow.js leaves. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2), differs: N2-122 A wrap break the port takes out types as a letter. Compared: Inserts and adjusts line feeds in the code buffer for the cell layout, with the patched spots 0xc5a18 / 0xc5a24. Part of the monospaced layout recorded as deliberately not adopted (NATIVE-PARITY.md:99-101); textbox.js addChars keeps the break characters that reflow.js leaves, and a line feed is no typed letter on either side. Fixed 2026-11-08 (N2-122): reflow.js writes a break it removes as textbox.js SOFT: a space on screen that is no letter of the typing (the raw line feed costs none, 0xbd990). Compared with the game 2026-11-09 (N2-122, TODO item 51): Native frames: in "...the night's cold\nair." at 6 ticks a letter the a of the second row comes one interval after the d (672-673 ticks against 666-667); the port's frames give 674 and 668.

feature: vtable init
font select
note: Sets a different font (+0x18bf0) for choice labels.

feature: clip rectangle
note: Clamps and stores a clip rectangle.

feature: glyph quad build
note: Builds glyph quads and the drop shadow (offset +0x18a58/+0x18a5c x 1.5) for the text; the web uses host fonts with a CSS shadow.

feature: text object draw
note: Draws the glyph buffer with the object's blend value (+0x18a64), colour and shadow pass.

feature: redraw callback
string callback
note: Vtable method of the font helper.

destructor

runtime tween/easing utility
note: Cited. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2), differs: N2-105 Mode panel slides out on the wrong curve. Compared: Returns start for t <= 0 and end for t >= duration or a bad type or mode; otherwise calls easing object type (table *0xae0178, 13 classes) with mode 0 in, 1 out, 2 in-out. touchfx.js rippleAt matches type 2 in (1 - u^2, 0xfe914) and type 3 out (0xfe9bc); ui.js setBack matches type 3 in-out (0xfe9e8) as EASE.cubic.inout; the mode panel's type 2 out over 20 frames is style.css cubic-bezier(1/3, 2/3, 2/3, 1); audio.js's 1.54 v - 0.54 v^2 is type 12 (0xff4b8) with control point 0.77. Fixed 2026-11-08 (N2-105): style.css: .modepanel closes on the reversed opening curve (ease-in, cubic-bezier(.333,0,.667,.333)); opening keeps ease-out. Listing and test; no native frame. Compared with the game 2026-11-09 (N2-105): Native frames of the mode panel closing, every present: the bar's lower edge is at 93 - 104 (n / 20)^2 px on tick n (92, 91, 89, 87, 84, 80, 72 at n = 9, 67, 62, 56, 49, 35 at n = 15, 18 at n = 17, 9), the quadratic the port's closing curve is; opening is the same curve the other way.

note: Stops the handle's old sound, StartInfo with the loop override byte, SetVolume(master x v) or 0 when fade frames>0, SetPan(p raw), pitch 1. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2), differs: N2-25 Sound system master scale 127/96 missing. Compared: Stops the handle's old sound, records id and time, starts with the StartInfo loop override from byte +0x39, then sets volume (0 when fade frames > 0 and the volume is above 0, else master x volume), pan, pitch and third axis; every caller passes pitch 1 and third axis 0. audio.js:playSE stops the channel's record, and node() / begin() start from gain 0 with the loop region and panMatrix, with schedule then placing the level. Fade frames of 0 with a fade-in needs an 001 of 2-16 ms, and SEPL's 001 values under 20 are only 0 and 1. Fixed 2026-11-08 (N2-25): audio.js applyVolumes, master = 96 / 127 x 127 / 96; measured on a native run's mix.

feature: wave sound start wrapper
note: -> 0xedd28. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2, traced twice): Bounds-checks the wave handle index (0 <= n < table +0x24), resolves the handle at table +0x20 + n, calls 0xedd28 and returns the handle's first field (-2 when out of range); the return value has no effect on sound. audio.js:node is reached with fixed handle slots from playSE and playSys, so no out-of-range path exists.

feature: wave handle stop
note: Stop(0). Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2, traced twice): Bounds-checks the wave handle, calls Stop(0) when a sound is attached and sets the handle's id to -1. audio.js:stopNode calls stop() on the source; callers are 0x9b700, 0xad060 at boot and the mixer's state-2 end.

stream start (music)
note: StartInfo loop byte, offset type 2 = samples (cited); SetVolume(1), pitch 1. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2), differs: N2-25 Sound system master scale 127/96 missing. Compared: Stops the handle's old sound, starts the stream with the loop byte override and, when 069 is non-zero, a start offset of type 2 (samples), at volume 1 and pitch 1; 0x9c470 / 0x9c6d0 set the real volume right after. audio.js:playBGM passes 069 / 48000 as the offset and the loop as a region from musicLoops; the 28 tracks with 069 all have it below their loop end, and all 128 streams are 48 kHz. Fixed 2026-11-08 (N2-25): audio.js applyVolumes, master = 96 / 127 x 127 / 96; measured on a native run's mix.

feature: stream handle stop
note: Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2, traced twice): Bounds-checks the stream handle, calls Stop(fade frames) and sets the id to -1; every caller (0x9b650 from 0x9c470, 0x9c610, 0x9c6d0, and the mixer) passes 0 frames. audio.js:stopNode stops the source at once.

feature: stream pause/resume
stream handle busy
stream loop byte
stream volume
note: master x v immediate; the curve is applied by its callers. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2), differs: N2-25 Sound system master scale 127/96 missing. Compared: Bounds-checks the stream handle, calls SetVolume(master x v, 0) and resets the handle's 0x30-byte value object through 0xec1d4 (its tween id -1, so 0xec24c leaves it idle; nothing applies it to the sound). audio.js:schedule sets v on the record's gain; the curve is applied in musicGain as in the callers. Fixed 2026-11-08 (N2-25): audio.js applyVolumes, master = 96 / 127 x 127 / 96; measured on a native run's mix.

feature: stream position ms
voice stream start
note: Volume as given (snd+9/100 linear), pan, pitch 1. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2), differs: N2-129 Voice Test shares interface sound slot 0; N2-25 Sound system master scale 127/96 missing. Compared: Starts a voice stream on voice handle n (table index +0x20 + +0x24 + n), stopping its old sound, with the given volume, pan 0, pitch 1 and third axis 0. audio.js:playVoice matches the story voices on handles 2 and 3; the second caller, the config's voice Test on handle 4 (0x2c1c4), is modelled in the port as an interface sound slot. Fixed 2026-11-08 (N2-25): audio.js applyVolumes, master = 96 / 127 x 127 / 96; measured on a native run's mix. N2-129 stays open.

feature: voice handle stop
note: Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2), differs: N2-129 Voice Test shares interface sound slot 0. Compared: Bounds-checks the voice handle, calls Stop(0), then resets two settings on the handle that was just stopped (no audible effect) and clears id, +0x2c, +0x30 and +0x38. audio.js:stopVoice covers handles 2 and 3 and stopTests the Test voice's stop.

feature: voice handle volume
note: Linear. Re-checked 2026-11-08 (N2), differs: N2-25 Sound system master scale 127/96 missing. Compared: Bounds-checks the voice handle, calls SetVolume(master x v, 0) or clears +0x38 when no sound is attached, and resets the idle value object through 0xec1d4. In the shipped game it is reached from 0x9d240 through 0x9b720 (the mixer's voice branch needs a level change and voices stay at 100, 0x9c300 being the only writer of a voice record's target); audio.js:applyVolumes sets the same row level on the current slot's gain, without the master scale. Fixed 2026-11-08 (N2-25): audio.js applyVolumes, master = 96 / 127 x 127 / 96; measured on a native run's mix.
